To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) halide coordination to the metal center plays a crucial role in determining the catechol like activity of monometallic nickel complexes with phenolic based ligand, (2) the ligand centered reduction of the complexes is the key step for the radical mechanism of the catalysis.
the catechol like activity of monomeric nickel(II) phenol based complexes is influenced by the halide ligands.

(i) mononuclear nickel complexes with phenol based tridendate ligands are good catalysts for the oxidation of 3, 5 di tert buty catechol (3 5 DTBC), and (ii) the activity depends on the nature of the halide counteranion, and (iii) chloride counteranion is not a good counteranion for such a reaction, as it coordinates to the metal in methanol solution and thus the reaction is not feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of halides in the catechol like activity of nickel complexes with a phenolic based ligand.
the effect of halide ligand on the catecholate activity of a nickel(II) complex with a phenol base tridentate ligands.
the effect of halide ligand on catecholase activity of mononuclea nickel(II) phenol based tridendate complex.

the presence of halide ligand(s) in the coordination sphere of the mononuclear nickel complex is a prerequisite for its catecholase-like activity, and the chloride ligand in 3 is not able to provide the required activity.
the presence of a protonated amine in the coordination environment of a nickel(II) center is a must for the catecholate oxidation by the metal center.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catechol like activity of monomeric nickel(II) complex depends on the halides coordinated to the metal.
the catechol like activity of a nickel complex is strongly influenced by the nature of the counter anion and the coordination chemistry of the complex.
we have synthesized three new mononuclear Ni(II) complexes of a phenol based ligand, and have studied the catechol like activity exhibited by these complexes.

the halide anion plays a key role in the catechol like activity of monometallic nickel(II) complex, and thus the role of halides in catalytic processes should be taken into consideration.
